lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: In an empty folder run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` route returning a small JSON object. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining a GET route at the root path
Server is up; open this URL

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
Path decorator for the HTTP GET method
Root path "/" calls the decorated function
uvicorn main:app syntax and --reload flag

hints: Install both packages: pip install fastapi uvicorn, then create main.py in your project folder.
In main.py: from fastapi import FastAPI, then app = FastAPI().
Add @app.get("/") above a function that returns a dict like {"Hello": "World"}.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder containing main.py, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and getting 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory, causing 'Could not import module "main"'.
Naming the instance something other than app but still running main:app (Attribute "app" not found).
Forgetting the @ on the decorator or the parentheses in FastAPI().
Using main.py:app instead of main:app.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add a module-level `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function taking `item: str` that appends it and returns the list. Test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Module-level list holding the items
New POST endpoint at /items
Server logged your POST request

explanations.topic: Endpoints handle HTTP POST requests to a path
A plain function argument becomes a query parameter
Returning the whole list to see results
Passing the item via ?item= in the URL

hints: Create an empty list at the top level of main.py, outside any function.
Decorate a new function with @app.post("/items") and give it a parameter `item: str`.
Inside the function, append item to the list and return the list.
Keep uvicorn running (with --reload) and, in a second terminal, run curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'.
common_mistakes: Defining items = [] inside the function, so the list resets on every request.
Using @app.get instead of @app.post, giving 405 Method Not Allowed for the curl POST.
Forgetting the ?item=... query parameter, which returns a 422 'field required' error.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so the ? or & is interpreted by the shell.
Server not restarted/reloaded after editing, so the new route returns 404.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item ID
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with a function taking `item_id: int` that returns `items[item_id]`. POST a couple of items again, then `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0`.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with an item_id path parameter
item_id typed as int indexes the items list
Request index 0 to get the first item

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly braces map URL segments to a variable
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value becomes the function argument of the same name
Type hint makes FastAPI convert the path value to int
Requesting a missing index causes an internal server error

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator as your hello world route, but put the variable part of the path in curly braces.
The name inside the braces must match the function parameter name, e.g. /items/{item_id} and def get_item(item_id: int).
Return items[item_id]; without the int type hint the value arrives as a string and list indexing fails.
After saving, the server reloads and empties the list: POST your items again before requesting /items/0.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to re-POST items after the auto-reload, so /items/0 returns an Internal Server Error (IndexError).
Leaving out the ': int' type hint, so item_id is a string and items[item_id] raises TypeError.
Mismatched names between the path placeholder {item_id} and the function parameter.
Writing the path without curly braces ("/items/item_id"), which creates a literal route instead of a parameter.
Requesting an index beyond the list length and assuming the code is broken (that 500 error is handled in the next step).

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py import HTTPException from fastapi and in get_item return the item only if item_id < len(items), otherwise raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...). Request a missing index with curl to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 when the item index is out of range
The request now returns a helpful 404 detail

explanations.topic: Checking whether the item exists before returning it
404 status code means the item was not found
Using the detail parameter to explain the error

hints: Add HTTPException to the same import line as FastAPI.
In get_item, only return items[item_id] when item_id < len(items).
In the else branch: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found").
Re-run the curl request with an index larger than your list to see {"detail": ...}.
common_mistakes: Using return HTTPException(...) instead of raise, which gives a 200 response or a serialization error instead of a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError.
Using <= instead of <, so item_id == len(items) still raises an IndexError (500).
Forgetting the f prefix on the detail string, so it literally shows {item_id}.
Not saving or reloading the server, so the old 500 error still appears.

steps.title: Add list endpoint with limit query
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. POST several items, then run `curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'` and confirm it prints a JSON list.

targets.caption: New list endpoint taking a limit query parameter
Server log line for the limited list request

explanations.topic: FastAPI converts query string values to the annotated type (int)
limit slices the items list; default 10 when omitted
Same /items path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value comes from the function signature

hints: Add a new function decorated with @app.get on the same "/items" path you used for POST.
Give the function a parameter like `limit: int = 10`; any parameter not in the path becomes a query parameter.
Return a slice of your list: `return items[0:limit]`.
Restart or let uvicorn reload, POST a few items first, then run curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3' (quote the URL so the shell doesn't treat ? specially).
common_mistakes: Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the request hits create_item instead of list_items.
Forgetting the `: int` annotation, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError.
Testing before adding any items (server restart clears the in-memory list), so the response is just [].
Not quoting the curl URL, so the shell mangles the ?limit=3 query string.
Writing items[limit] instead of items[0:limit], returning one item or an IndexError.

steps.title: Use a Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: In main.py import BaseModel from pydantic, define class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, make create_item take item: Item and get_item return -> Item. POST JSON with curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' and see the object in the response.

targets.caption: Pydantic model with text and is_done
create_item now takes the model from the JSON body
Response is an object matching the Item model

explanations.topic: Extending BaseModel to define the Item fields
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not query params
Default value is_done = False appears in the response
Removing a default makes the field required and validated

hints: Define a class that inherits from pydantic's BaseModel with a str field and a bool field defaulting to False.
Change the create_item parameter's type from str to your model so FastAPI reads it from the request body.
Send the data as JSON: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items (no ?item= query).
If it returns 422, check the JSON key matches your field name and the Content-Type header is set.
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter (?item=apple), which now gives a 422 error.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header.
Using double quotes around the -d payload in bash without escaping the inner quotes.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not using --reload), so the old string-based endpoint still runs.
Giving text a default value, so a payload without text doesn't fail validation.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Restart uvicorn and confirm the endpoints still return Item-shaped JSON.

targets.caption: Single item response model on get_item
List response model on list_items

explanations.topic: Using a Pydantic BaseModel to describe responses
response_model argument on the route decorator
Response model for a list of items
Response models declare the endpoint's output contract

hints: The response model goes in the route decorator, not in the function signature.
Add a keyword argument after the path: @app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=Item).
For the list endpoint wrap the model in a list type: response_model=list[Item].
Save the file and make sure uvicorn reloads with no Traceback in the terminal.
common_mistakes: Writing response_model on the function instead of inside @app.get(...)
Using list[Item] on Python < 3.9 instead of typing.List[Item]
Passing an instance like Item() instead of the class Item
Returning data that does not match the Item fields, which causes a validation error on the response
Forgetting the comma between the path string and response_model

steps.title: Explore interactive docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, click 'Try it out' on POST /items and Execute. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click 'Try it out' on the POST endpoint
Send the request and inspect the response body
Small link to the raw OpenAPI JSON schema

explanations.topic: Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Try it out / Execute sends a real request and shows the curl command
/redoc is an alternative documentation view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses

hints: Make sure uvicorn is still running, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint and click 'Try it out' to make the request body editable.
Edit the JSON body to match your Item model, then click 'Execute' and scroll down to 'Server response'.
Also try /redoc, and click the small /openapi.json link under the title to see the raw schema.
common_mistakes: Server not running (or stopped) so /docs fails to load.
Typing /doc or /docs/ variants incorrectly instead of /docs.
Request body JSON not matching the Pydantic model, giving a 422 Unprocessable Entity response.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out' first, so the body can't be edited.
